example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, 8999 Uncategorized Expense and one bank statement file, September 2026. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

messages.text: Can you code our September transactions? A lot of them are still uncategorized.
Yes. Before I read anything, I need seven answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
Which transactions do you want coded? With MosoFin, I can find the ones in your uncategorized and suspense accounts.
Do you want tax codes? If yes, for which country, and which tax codes do you use?
Above what amount do you record a purchase as an asset, not as an expense? Ask your accountant if you are not sure. If you leave it blank, I flag large equipment purchases for you.
Optional: do you have house rules that override what you did in the past?
Optional: what are the names of the owners, their family on the books and their other businesses? I use them only for a flag.

messages.text: Use MosoFin and find them. Northbrook Trading. Yes to tax codes, US, the codes in our books. Our limit is $2,500. Phone and internet always go to 6340. I also own Lindqvist Property.

messages.label: Found your workspace and company file

messages.text: I found one workspace, **Northbrook Trading**, with one company file of the same name. Is that the right one?

Here is my plan. I code the **38 transactions in 8999 Uncategorized Expense** at **Northbrook Trading** against your chart and your coding history. Tax codes come from your list, and you confirm which one applies. Your limit is **$2,500**, and phone and internet go to 6340.
messages.after: Bank-feed items that wait for review are not in the ledger yet. Upload the statement file if you want those coded too. Shall I start?

messages.text: Yes. Here is the bank file. It has one more item.

messages.label: Checked the tools, then read the books
messages.summary: 10 calls and your file. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: Most rows are clear. 26 of the 39 have a consistent history and no flag. For example, I strip the Square prefix from "SQ *HARBOR OFFICE SUPPLY". Your history puts that vendor in 6520 in 23 of 24 payments. But a history shows your habit. It does not prove that the habit is correct:
messages.after: Brightwave is a split, so I do not pick a side. Your rule picks 6340, and I report that the history disagrees. TechDepot is consistent, but this row is a laptop and a monitor. It is $650 above your $2,500 limit, so I flag it as a possible asset. You and your accountant decide.

messages.text: Two rows are not expenses or income. I name both legs, so you do not count anything twice:

card.title: Money that only moves
head: Row
Amount
What I found
rows: A transfer. +4,200.00 arrives on the card on Mon 28 Sep
39 Stripe, from your bank file, Tue 29 Sep

messages.after: Your sales are already in the books. If I coded the Stripe payout as income, I would count the same sales two times.

messages.text: These rows need a decision from you. I conclude nothing about them:

card.title: For your review
head: Row
Amount
Why
rows: No hosting account in your chart. The nearest is 6330
Loan payment. The interest part needs the lender statement
Germany. You choose the tax code
Possible personal. What was the business purpose?
Rent to your other business. Related party

messages.after: Row 11 has no payee at all. Its bank text is only POS DEBIT 0034871, so I do not guess. I put the whole loan payment on 2700 Bank Loan until you have the lender statement.

messages.text: Here is the whole batch. 26 rows are High, 9 are Medium and 4 are Low. 9 rows have a flag.
messages.after: High is 66.7% of the rows, Medium 23.1% and Low 10.3%. They add to 100.1% because I round each one.

messages.text: Looks good. Just post them all.
I cannot do that. I never write to your books. The coded list is a draft, and a person posts it in your accounting system.
messages.after: Do you want the list as an Excel file? It also has the Uncoded Population and Coverage sheets.

messages.text: Done. Here is **Northbrook Trading_Coded_Transactions_2026-10-05.xlsx**. Its header says that I read your chart from the books.
messages.after: Do you want me to save your coding rules for next month?

messages.text: Done. For Northbrook Trading, I saved your phone and internet rule, the $2,500 limit, the tax code mapping and the vendor rules you confirmed. I never save the transactions, the amounts or the Lindqvist flag.
